title: Flip M4-B accessibility and browser acceptance matrix
reason: No M4 web application exists on the accepted M3 baseline. No browser test in this matrix was run, and no passing result is claimed.

scenarios.name: Keyboard-only operation
scenarios.preconditions: M4 web app reachable; sample available; no pointer input used.
steps: Tab from the document start through Start, Import, Compose, Compare, Results and Export.
Activate every primary control with Enter or Space.
Complete J01 from sample selection through evidence download using only the keyboard.
passCriteria: Every primary action is reachable and operable without a pointer.
No keyboard trap; focus can leave every region.
Download is triggered by a keyboard-activatable control with a descriptive name.

scenarios.name: Focus order and focus visibility
scenarios.preconditions: Same as B01; include modal/error states.
steps: Traverse the import form and pin-mapping table, recording the focus order.
Trigger WRONG_CHAIN and RPC_UNAVAILABLE states and observe focus placement.
Inspect the focus indicator at every stop for visible contrast.
passCriteria: Focus order follows reading order and never jumps behind a dialog.
After a validation error, focus moves to an error summary or the offending field.
A visible focus indicator is present in every focusable element.

scenarios.name: Accessible labels
scenarios.preconditions: Import form and composition table rendered.
steps: Inspect accessible names of processor, circuit ID, chain, pin and output-map controls.
Check that numbered pins expose index and width as text, not only position.
Verify every icon-only control has an accessible name.
passCriteria: No unlabelled form control or unnamed icon button.
Pin indices and bit widths are exposed in the accessibility tree.
Semantic pin names are either absent or visibly marked user-supplied.

scenarios.name: Screen-reader-friendly result announcements
scenarios.preconditions: Sample comparison produces DIFFERENT then EQUIVALENT.
steps: With a screen reader running, run the sample comparison.
Observe the announcement of verdict, freshness, oracle/intent and witness presence.
Open the counterexample table and navigate it by row and column.
passCriteria: A polite live region announces 'Result: DIFFERENT' and separately 'Freshness: HISTORICAL'.
Verdict is not conveyed by colour or icon alone.
Witness table has row and column headers and labelled bit indices.

scenarios.name: Responsive layout
steps: Render each journey step at each viewport.
Check pin-mapping table, witness table and report header for overflow.
Operate primary controls at 320 px without horizontal scrolling of the document.
passCriteria: No loss of content or function at 320 px; tables reflow or scroll within their labelled region.
Verdict, freshness and intent remain visible without scrolling sideways.
Touch targets meet minimum size where touch is supported.

scenarios.name: Loading and error states
scenarios.preconditions: Configurable slow/failing stub for import and compare.
steps: Trigger a slow import, a WRONG_CHAIN, an RPC_UNAVAILABLE and an INVALID_INPUT case.
Observe progress text, cancellability and the error message structure.
Verify that entered project state is preserved after each failure.
passCriteria: Loading is described in text, not only by a spinner.
Errors match the plain-language catalogue and expose technical details in a disclosure.
Project inputs and focus context survive the error.

scenarios.name: Timeouts
scenarios.preconditions: Comparison request with 1 ms solver deadline (C06 fixture).
steps: Run the comparison and watch the progress state transition to UNKNOWN.
Check the reason code is exposed as text and no EQUIVALENT badge appears.
Retry with an allowed higher deadline and confirm a normal result.
passCriteria: Text reads 'Inconclusive — solver timed out' with SOLVER_TIMEOUT in technical details.
No success styling or equivalent language is used.
A subsequent completed job succeeds, showing worker cleanup.

scenarios.name: Repeated workflow execution
scenarios.preconditions: Sample project ready; runs are repeatable.
steps: Run compose/compare five times consecutively in the browser.
Compare the displayed digest, verdict and freshness across runs.
Confirm no duplicate live-region announcements or stale result fragments remain.
passCriteria: All five runs show the same audited digest and verdict class.
Previous results are replaced, not accumulated.
Focus and announcements remain stable across repeats.

scenarios.name: Browser refresh and project recovery
scenarios.preconditions: Project state stored locally; refresh and quota errors can be simulated.
steps: Enter identities and a pin map, refresh the page, and observe restoration.
Explicitly reset and confirm the action.
Fill local storage to quota and observe the failure message.
passCriteria: Unsaved work survives an ordinary refresh with a visible restored-state notice.
Reset requires confirmation and cannot be triggered accidentally.
Quota failure is reported in text and does not silently discard work.

scenarios.name: Export accessibility
scenarios.preconditions: A completed comparison and a planned M4 export action.
steps: Inspect the export control name, the generated file name and the confirmation text.
Open the human-readable summary and verify it has headings, lists and table headers.
Check that no status is conveyed only by colour and that no secrets appear in the bundle.
passCriteria: Export is keyboard operable with a descriptive name including the file format.
Human-readable summary is navigable by headings and has labelled tables.
Verification status and freshness remain separate text labels after re-import.

scenarios.name: Pre-flight status separation
scenarios.preconditions: Planned M4 pre-flight UI with stubbed read-only responses.
steps: Run pre-flight with STRUCTURALLY ACCEPTED, REJECTED and UNKNOWN stubs.
Compare the presentation with a verification verdict on the same screen.
Check that 'no transaction broadcast' and the observed fee are visible.
passCriteria: Pre-flight status never reuses the EQUIVALENT/DIFFERENT/UNKNOWN verification badge.
UNKNOWN pre-flight is not styled as success.
No wallet, signing or broadcast control is present.
